lever: modtests: one line appended to the Rules of prompts/system.md: after the first edit to a module, run its test file once (tests/test_<module>.py, or the file git grep -l finds for the module name under tests/), even if the issue's example already passes; a failure there in code you changed is yours to fix before you submit.
tokens_added: 64 Gemma tokens (the model's tokenizer.json; v13's prompt is 840)
why: Mechanism (traces): p4_b1024, the run on v13's prompt line, grepped 'def is_interactive' (call 3, 18 s), found nothing because the name is an attribute assigned in Console.__init__, and added a @property of that name at call 17 (160 s); every Console construction then raises 'property ... has no setter'. It kept editing live.py/progress.py to call 39 and submitted at 287 s with 0 test runs. Measured offline: the module's own existing test file (tests/test_console.py, no hidden tests) on that patch gives 95 failed, 3 passed in 2.1 s, first error naming the new property (scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_modtests.py). The run had already mirrored the sibling's 0/1 values, so the regression is the only thing between it and the fix. p4_v0t2 solved it because it grepped the bare name (call 17) and edited the existing attribute; it ran no test either (13 s to spare). Evidence: docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_modtests.txt. The same rule covers rich_3278 p4_v0t2 (hidden tests 16/16, 3 existing broken) and rich_3180 p4_v7d (4/4, 4 existing broken), both visible in the module test file in under 0.3 s. Applies outside the 42: rich_3521's failing p4_v0t2 patch breaks 14 of the 52 tests in tests/test_segment.py (all 52 pass at base; measured with scripts/forty_two/rich_solve/ev_modtests_any.py), and p4_b1024 solves that task.
alternative: submissions/v13_flagvals (same commit): addresses the other failure family here: p4, p4_v7 and p4_v7c implemented only TTY_INTERACTIVE=0 although all six runs had the named sibling's 0/1 parse on screen by call 2-4; the 0/1/else-auto convention passes the hidden test and 0-only fails it (measured, docs/forty_two/evidence/rich_solve_flagvals.txt). Queue it for this id if v13_modtests fails with 0-only patches.
expected: maybe-to-likely if v13 behaves like p4_b1024 (right values, broken Console); no help if it writes a 0-only patch (existing tests pass with that)
baseline: p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024) failed; p4_v0t2 (v0-think) solved at 289 s; 4 of 12 Kaggle L4 runs solved
regression_risk: One extra call (about 5-8 s of model time plus the test run) after the first edit, on every task. Solved tasks it could hurt: those solved at the time cap through the fallback patch on p4_b1024 (rich_3521, rich_3506, fastapi_14794, fastapi_14458, fastapi_5624, fastapi_5077 at 304-305 s): the first edit has already landed when the extra call runs, so only later edits move; and tasks whose module test file already fails at base (rich_3278's base suite has 55 failures in 13 files, e.g. tests/test_table.py 16), where the model may chase failures it did not cause. fastapi test files are per feature, so the git grep -l form can return several files (60 s command timeout and the never-the-whole-suite rule still apply). Inferred, not measured.
box_risk: The base, submissions/v13, may carry a regression (coordinator, 2026-10-14): on the v13 box screen fastapi_14487 put its first tool call in the message text in Gemma's native syntax and made 0 tool calls; suspected cause is v13's fenced multi-line heredoc in step 3, which this bundle inherits unchanged. The added line has no fenced block, backtick, brace or tool-call-shaped text (pinned by tests/test_v13_rich_solve.py). A sample that ends with 0 tool calls points at the base, not at this lever.
